<action type="say">
Turn off the water and limit damage first, then I’ll help get an emergency plumber there.

1) Stop the water:
- Look behind or beside the toilet for a small shutoff valve on the wall or floor. Turn it clockwise all the way until it stops.
- If you can’t find or turn that valve, open the toilet tank and lift the float (the balloon/float cup) straight up to stop water from refilling. Wedge something under it if you can so it stays up.
- As a last resort, if you know where your main water shutoff is for the home, turn that off.

2) Make it safe:
- Unplug or move any electrical items on the floor or near the water.
- If water is near outlets or power strips on the floor and you can safely reach your breaker panel without stepping in water, switch off power to that bathroom.

3) Contain the mess:
- Use towels, rags, or a mop to keep water from spreading to other rooms or under walls/door frames.
- If you have a bucket, gently bail excess water from the toilet bowl into a sink or tub (if draining normally), but only if the bowl is still very full and not draining.

Next, I can get an emergency plumber to you. Please reply with:
- Your full address (or at least city and ZIP/postal code)
- Whether the water is still actively rising or has stopped
- Any constraints (apartment building, need someone within a certain time window, etc.)
</action>
